name: Grassy Green
lede: Grassy Green is a sharp, yellow-leaning green named for grass itself, recorded by the 2010 xkcd color-name survey and barely distinguishable from the older name Grass Green.

sections.title: Named for the plant underfoot
sections.body:
Our library traces Grassy Green to the xkcd color survey of 2010, an online project that asked visitors to type a name for colors shown on screen and kept the names enough of them agreed on [1]. The name itself is plain: grass, the plant, plus the color word [[green]] [1].

It sits close enough to [[grass-green|Grass Green]], an older and more common name for nearly the same hue, that the two are only 0.6 color-distance units apart, closer than most eyes can tell on a screen [2]. The nearest other named look-alikes on file are [[true-green|True Green]] and [[leaf-green|Leaf Green]], both a touch lighter [2]. In print, the two-word phrase "grassy green" was already common by the early 1800s and peaked around 1820, close to two centuries before the survey logged it as a single color name [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color close enough to this one over enough of its canvas to count, as photographed [4]. That says more about the collection, weighted toward European and pre-modern museum holdings, than about where the color turns up in the world, which is mostly fresh grass under bright light [4].
